title: Does ECHO's embodied plasticity improve adaptive behaviour under locomotor impairment, and where?
question: Under a walking impairment, does a research fly running echo-embodied-plasticity/v2 in active mode take in more energy, or feed more often, than the same organism without it, by at least the minimum meaningful effect; can any difference be attributed to learning rather than to slowing as such; and where, across unseen impairments, food layouts and energy states, does any effect hold, vanish or reverse?
hypotheses: Confirmatory (two-sided): in weak-legs, plasticity-active minus organism differs from zero in energy taken in (fedJ) and in feeding bouts (meals). The decision rule, not the sign, decides what is claimed.
Mechanism: if the plasticity helps, it helps through learned timing, so in weak-legs plasticity-active should beat fixed-slow (the same slowing always) as well as the organism.
Boundary: where the plasticity never becomes cautious (unimpaired, mild impairment, asymmetric gait) it cannot act, so plasticity-active should equal the organism exactly there.

Stated before any run of this protocol: given the 2026-11-07 held-out study, the expected outcome is NO_DEMONSTRATED_IMPROVEMENT or INCONCLUSIVE. The protocol is built to measure that accurately, not to overturn it.
priorKnowledge: The 2026-11-07 held-out study (docs/benchmarks/echo-plasticity/heldout, commit 288b3a8, 24 seeds): in weak-legs, active minus original meals +0.17 (95% CI -1.00 to 1.33), fedJ -0.012 J (95% CI -0.056 to 0.031): no difference established. Active mode acted in every weak-legs run and in no other condition. Shadow mode was identical to the organism in 144 of 144 runs.
That study's dev split (seeds 9001-9008) set the minimum meaningful effects below: the organism's mean in weak-legs was 1.283 J taken in and 10.0 meals.

Sample size: with the earlier held-out's standard deviation of paired differences (fedJ 0.112 J, meals 2.93), 40 subjects give a 97.5% interval half-width near 0.04 J for fedJ (a third of its minimum meaningful effect) and near 1.0 for meals (equal to its minimum meaningful effect), so meals may stay INCONCLUSIVE whatever the truth.

Weak legs (speedGain 0.35) also slow flight (perturbation.ts), and the fly travels mostly by air: in the earlier study the organism's intake fell only from 1.280 J (moving food) to 1.227 J (weak legs). The assay-sensitivity check below measures whether each impairment costs the baseline anything at all.
The candidate is not tuned here: echo-embodied-plasticity/v2 is evaluated exactly as merged in PR #178. Nothing in the controllers changes between the dev and held-out splits.
experimentalUnit: A research subject: one seed in one condition, born once per controller from the same genesis (seed, start heading, food schedule, perturbation schedule and the fly's random streams), so every comparison is a paired difference per subject. Simulation ticks are never units.

conditions.description: Food moves to the next compass site every 20 simulated minutes; no perturbation. The reference for every assay-sensitivity check.
From minute 10 the body advances 35% as far as its legs step (and its wings hold 35% of the commanded speed): the 2026-11-07 study's weak-legs, on new subjects.
A milder impairment: speedGain 0.6, above the plasticity's 0.4 progress share, so its walks should still count as effective.
Asymmetric movement: from minute 10 every walking and flying turn is biased by 0.8 rad/s (turnBias), with full speed.
An unseen combination: weak legs (0.35) and, at the same time, a self-motion sense four times as noisy, which corrupts the evidence the plasticity learns from.
The impairment ends: weak legs (0.35) from minute 10 to minute 50, then a sound body for 70 minutes. Tests whether learned caution outlives its cause.
Weak legs (0.35) in a fly that starts at 20% of its reserve, so its walks are first judged in the plasticity's low-energy context.
Different geometry: food between the compass sites, 6.5 m out and away from every pole, with weak legs (0.35).

confirmatory.mmeRule: 10% of the organism's mean energy taken in under weak legs in the 2026-11-07 dev split (1.283 J), rounded down to 0.128 J: the smallest change in two hours' intake this protocol treats as meaningful. A model choice, fixed before any run.

10% of the organism's mean meals under weak legs in the 2026-11-07 dev split (10.0): one feeding bout in two hours. The 2026-11-07 study's own primary endpoint, replicated on new subjects. A model choice, fixed before any run.

analysis.estimator: mean paired difference over research subjects (candidate minus reference), with dz and an exact sign test

rules: Per comparison: REGRESSION when the interval lies wholly on the worse side of zero; IMPROVEMENT when it lies wholly on the better side and the mean reaches the minimum meaningful effect δ; NO_DEMONSTRATED_IMPROVEMENT when it lies wholly inside (-δ, +δ); otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.

Overall: INVALID if any validity check fails (incomplete design, a record bound to another protocol, any failed run, an unpaired environment, a validity controller that differs from the baseline, or a subject that is not a research subject). Else REGRESSION if a confirmatory endpoint regresses; IMPROVEMENT if one improves and no confirmatory endpoint or guardrail regresses; INCONCLUSIVE if one improves while a guardrail regresses; REGRESSION if none improves and a guardrail regresses; NO_DEMONSTRATED_IMPROVEMENT if every confirmatory endpoint is NO_DEMONSTRATED_IMPROVEMENT; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
Secondary contrasts carry no claims. Internal measures (detection, self-model accuracy) never decide a behavioural verdict.

stopping: Every unit of a split runs once. The held-out split runs once, from a clean commit, after the dev split's records are committed; no interim look, no rerun, no replacement of a failed run. A failed or inconclusive held-out result stays in the record.
